item.text:
Completed bounded continuation for the only currently selected chapter, 1B, covering all lenses 1B.1–1B.10.

The chapter gained five new source-claim units:

- `WEB065` — Brazil’s 2022 IAEA statement describes the sector as safeguarded, records establishment of the independent ANSN regulator, and notes ratification of the physical-protection amendment. Institutional continuity; indirect Bolsonaro-period attribution. [IAEA statement, pp. 1–2](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/22/09/brazil-gc66.pdf)

- `WEB066` — The same statement records Brazil’s May 2022 negotiations with the IAEA for special safeguards procedures covering naval nuclear propulsion, while affirming NPT compliance and the Quadripartite Agreement. This establishes a genuine dual-use governance issue, not proliferation. [IAEA statement, p. 2](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/22/09/brazil-gc66.pdf)

- `WEB067` — Brazil’s Defense Ministry records continuing adherence to the NPT, Tlatelolco, and nuclear-weapons prohibition regimes, and states that constitutional and ABACC safeguards constrain non-peaceful nuclear activity. Persistent institutional baseline applicable during 2022; not personal credit. [Defense Ministry treaty summary](https://www.gov.br/defesa/pt-br/assuntos/relacoes-internacionais/foruns-internacionais-1/tratados-e-regimes)

- `WEB068` — On 30 December 2022, Bolsonaro personally sanctioned legislation restructuring uranium-mineral research, mining, and commercialization while retaining INB’s constitutional monopoly and citing strengthened nuclear safety and environmental protection. Direct formal attribution for policy action; no weapons or proliferation finding. [Presidential sanction record, lines 184–206](https://www.gov.br/secretariageral/pt-br/noticias/2022/dezembro/presidente-sanciona-projeto-de-lei-de-conversao-que-trata-sobre-a-empresa-industrias-nucleares-do-brasil-s-a-inb)

- `WEB069` — A September 2022 Angra event released up to 90 liters of water containing artificial radionuclides after a valve failure. CNEN found no population or environmental risk, but reported that the operator had not promptly notified the regulator and issued a corrective notification requirement. Target-period adverse safety event; published retrospectively in 2023 and not attributable to Bolsonaro personally. [CNEN report, lines 174–183](https://www.gov.br/crcnne/pt-br/assuntos/noticias/nota-de-esclarecimento-sobre-vazamento-na-usina-de-angra)

Targeted and contrary searches covered nuclear weapons, threats, proliferation, naval command changes, submarine safeguards, nuclear incidents, radioactive releases, IAEA compliance, dual-use governance, and catastrophic-risk events. No evidence was recovered of a Bolsonaro nuclear threat, weapons decision, near-use episode, command change, proliferation act, or catastrophic nuclear-risk decision.

Honest shortfall: 1B remains attribution-limited. The recoverable record now supports institutional nuclear exposure, safeguards, regulatory design, naval-propulsion governance, one bounded safety incident, and one directly attributed civilian nuclear-minerals policy action. It still does not establish ruler-specific nuclear responsibility across the chapter.
